rubrics.justification: Mostly consistent with a good-quality blastocyst and visible ICM/blastocoel, but it overstates TE as uniformly cohesive and calls the embryo fully expanded/thinning zona more confidently than the image alone supports.
Integrates age, tubal factor, ovarian reserve, prior live birth, endometrium, BMI, and sperm parameters well with embryo quality, though some links (e.g., BMI significance) are somewhat overstated.

Reasoning is logical and internally consistent, with a plausible prognosis tied to embryo quality and patient factors; minor overreach around euploidy prediction and prior failed cycle interpretation.

Recommendations are broadly aligned with IVF practice, especially SET in a young patient with a good blastocyst; slight deviation in suggesting PGT-A after a single failure in a young patient and in implying ultrasound alone can rule out hydrosalpinx.

Provides clear practical steps for transfer and future planning, including SET and hydrosalpinx consideration, though some advice is somewhat generic and not deeply individualized beyond standard care.
